National Laboratory of the Rockies | 13 Types of NGVs Types of NGVs • Heavy-duty NGVs, as well as many medium-duty models, are available from original equipment manufacturers (OEMs). • NGVs are categorized into three configurations: ◦ Dedicated: Vehicles run exclusively on natural gas. ◦ Bi-fuel: Vehicles have two separate fuel systems and can operate on either natural gas or gasoline. ◦ Dual-fuel: Vehicles that operate primarily on natural gas with diesel fuel used for ignition assistance; typically limited to heavy- duty applications. Photo: GRTC Transit System • Vehicles may also be converted for natural gas operation by qualified system retrofitters. • Additional information about natural gas vehicles. Source: Alternative Fuels Data Center, Natural Gas Vehicles, n.d. National Laboratory of the Rockies | 14 Propane Propane • Propane is the third most common transportation fuel worldwide, behind gasoline and diesel. • Also referred to as liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) or propane autogas. • Propane is stored as a colorless, odorless liquid under pressure in a tank. • When pressure is released, the liquid propane vaporizes into a gas that is used in combustion. Photo: Matthew Jeffers, NREL Source: Alternative Fuels Data Center, Propane Fuel Basics, n.d.
